title: Rite of the Guardian Spirit
summary: A level four mystic rite that gives a sept its totem.

claims.text: The rite makes a spirit the totem of a whole sept; the details change with the spirit, but it always opens with a rich sacrifice to catch the spirit’s notice.

Next, champions prove the sept’s worth to suit the spirit: ritual combat with a captured Bane for a Totem of War, a play of an old Garou victory for a Totem of Respect, or a formal debate on the Litany for a Totem of Wisdom or Cunning.
A successful rite closes with a second, greater offering.

title: Caern shrines
summary: Where a sept honours its spirits.

claims.text: Septs keep shrines to the totems of their tribes and packs, and some to further spirits of the local court too, gathered in one place or scattered across the caern.
In old caerns some shrines honour spirits no living member remembers; wise septs keep worshipping there and guess at fitting offerings, while careless ones let them decay.
Every sept’s living area includes some place for public assembly, even if only a cleared dining hall.
A water-current spirit bound into a stethoscope senses where a city’s life moves, since cities clog like arteries.
Pressing it to a permanent building and rolling Perception + Streetwise at difficulty 6 shows whether the city’s roads, utilities or navigable waterways are blocked or cut, and roughly where.

title: The Chernobyl Exclusion Zone
summary: A Wyrm victory reclaimed by animals.

claims.text: Animals have taken back the abandoned zone, among them close to two thousand wolves with few natural threats.
Garou see it as living in the shadow of a great Wyrm victory: the radiation remains, a simple wildfire can spread fresh fallout, and many animals carry mutations such as sterility.
Their numbers are up only because humans no longer hunt or fish there, and the radiation caps how much life the land can hold.

title: Rite of the Hearthfire
summary: A level one caern rite of the Nenets.

claims.text: Garou among the Nenets people, who are few, teach this rite to gifted Kinfolk: a fire and some quiet blessings make a small shelter from the elements.

After building the fire, roll Wits + Rites at difficulty 7; success makes a bubble for three people plus one per success, lasting the night, keeping out snow, wind and rain and making the ground warm enough to sleep on.
A level three version covers an area the size of a caern’s bawn.
